note: Reviewed per-tool policy draft for the HOL-Guard MCP server contribution of duckdb-vectors. This is a staging reference captured in this repository; the canonical review.json is produced and bound inside a HOL-Guard checkout via `hol-guard extensions generate`. States: allow | review | block | inherit. Both exposed tools are read-only; MCP annotations are absent (annotations: null), so classification is justified from the server source, not from any readOnlyHint.

tools.name: search
tools.rationale: Read-only hybrid retrieval over the local DuckDB index. Takes a query string and top_k and returns ranked chunks; it opens a VectorStore and calls store.query(), which only reads. No write, delete, index rebuild, embedding-model mutation, filesystem write, or network call occurs on this tool path. Classification is drawn from the server source, not from any annotation (none is published).

tools.name: report
tools.rationale: Read-only introspection of the index: returns db_path, backend, dimensions, chunk count, and the sorted list of sources. It reads catalog/metadata only and mutates nothing. Caveat: the sources field discloses the folder-relative file paths that were indexed, so report() reveals index structure (not document contents) to a caller; this is disclosure, not mutation, and does not change the read-only classification.

notExposedOverMcp: Indexing (including the `mcp --index <folder>` startup build), writes, deletes, and embedding/model operations are CLI/SDK-level, not MCP tools. The startup index runs once in run_stdio before serving and is not a callable tool, so it carries no per-tool MCP policy here.
